inputs.original_text: After years of a system that left ordinary Cubans with little property and too little money to buy the businesses still functioning, a political transition could leave them shut out once again. Wealthy members of the diaspora—and possibly foreign investors—may be positioned to buy up property at bargain prices while Cuban residents watch their own country pass into other hands. A real transition should put Cuban families and local ownership first, not turn the island into a clearance sale for those with money.
inputs.modified_text: Cuba’s communist system has left ordinary people without the property or money needed to rebuild their lives. A transition that lets wealthy diaspora buyers and foreign investors scoop up Cuban property at bargain prices would only replace one form of dispossession with another. Cuban families and local ownership must come first; a nation’s future should not be handed to whoever arrives with the deepest pockets.
